top_stories.title: AI agents used to hack 100+ companies via exposed, password-free control panels
points: A Chinese-speaking hacker used Cairn, an open-source AI agent tool, to breach 100+ companies including Cummins, Deere, and SharkNinja with minimal human intervention.

Attacker left 20+ Cairn control panels (dashboards coordinating AI agents) exposed online with no password, feeding agents a pre-screened list of 1,000+ online stores and simple attack instructions under 100 characters.

Success rate was roughly 10% of attempts, each taking about 23 hours start-to-finish; cost was approximately $50 per successful breach (or ~$5 per attempt averaged across failures) using Claude Code and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.

Exposed dashboards contained unencrypted target lists, stolen credentials, and still-valid API keys; one compromised hardware parts vendor had an active backdoor (hidden server page allowing file uploads) still live.

Companies' containment status is unclear: SharkNinja says threat contained, Deere cites remediation actions, Cummins says it's investigating; NorForge is working with Reuters to notify victims and take down dashboards.

unique_angles.point: One attacker group had a bug that corrupted site names (e.g., 'wholesale' became 'holesale'), inadvertently making their panels easier to track.
Businesses advised to audit login systems and file upload pages, and to verify any hired security red teams aren't leaving their own dashboards exposed.
Attack used Cairn alongside a pre-screened list of over 1,200 online stores, specifically targeting named firms Cummins, Deere, and SharkNinja.

top_stories.title: Mercury 3: ultra-fast diffusion language model from Inception Labs
points: Mercury 3 is a 'diffusion' language model (generates and refines multiple words simultaneously, unlike traditional models that write one word at a time) that outputs 1,000+ tokens per second.
It matches or beats OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna and Anthropic's Claude Haiku 5.5 at 4-8x their speed, priced at $0.20/$0.70 per million tokens.
Despite being 40x larger than Inception's earlier Mercury 1 model, it maintains the same generation speed, suggesting diffusion models can scale without hitting algorithmic speed limits.
Early adopters are using it for real-time tutoring, voice customer support, and web-browsing agents where latency (response delay) is highly visible to users.

unique_angles.point: An independent tester (Corey Noles) ran Mercury 3 at a total cost of about $0.04 for his test.
Mercury 3 uses an iterative generation process similar to image diffusion models, and exceeds performance of larger competitors on standard evaluations.

top_stories.title: DHS bans DeepSeek from federal civilian agency systems
points: Department of Homeland Security formally ordered removal of DeepSeek products from federal civilian agency systems over security concerns.
The ban extends to any third-party tools built on top of the Chinese lab's models, per CISA directive.

top_stories.title: Anthropic co-founder declares AI 'singularity' has begun
points: Jack Clark told IMF and World Bank leaders that AI has entered a 'singularity' phase (a point where AI-driven progress outpaces human ability to track or control it) based on breakthroughs in expert-level reasoning.
Evidence cited: AI scores on the Humanity's Last Exam benchmark rose from 8% to 67.7% since 2025, and FrontierMath scores improved to 94%.
One Anthropic economic model predicts U.S. GDP could reach $44 trillion by 2030 if AI adoption accelerates rapidly, though Clark called this 'outlandish' and warned of 'very disruptive' job impacts.
Clark and CEO Dario Amodei are pushing for policy guardrails, including limits on AI's maximum allowed capability level, saying only a 'small number of years' remain to decide.

unique_angles.point: Frames the singularity claim alongside existing systems (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) already solving complex math, biology, and robotics problems as supporting evidence, and ties it to a need for major infrastructure investment and governance.

items.title: MiniMax M3.1 Flash boosts speed and cuts costs for agentic tasks
points: Achieves 3x faster inference and a 70% cost reduction for agentic tasks compared to prior versions.
Supports coding, Computer Use (automated systems controlling digital interfaces), and cybersecurity applications.
Now available through the MiniMax API and Code platform.

items.title: Cloudflare's Clairic introduces hallucination-free 'extraction model'
points: Clairic returns direct values from unstructured input data rather than generating tokens, avoiding the hallucination risks common in large language models (LLMs).
Outputs include confidence scores to indicate reliability of extracted values.

items.title: Exa 3.0 launches as large-scale independent search engine
points: New Exa Lite tier priced at $4 per 1,000 requests.
Maintains an independent crawler and index spanning 2 trillion URLs and 100 billion pages.
Includes 1.27 billion ecommerce listings with real-time pricing/availability and 211 million local businesses with hours and ratings.

items.title: Meta's Prometheus supercluster scales toward 1 million GPUs
points: Uses closed-loop liquid cooling to support gigawatt-scale AI training.
Designed to train Meta's Muse model family at this massive scale.

items.title: AI benchmarking faces 'benchmaxxing' risks
points: Industry benchmarks increasingly shape model training but risk steering development toward optimizing for the metric rather than real-world performance ('benchmaxxing').
Avoiding misleading progress signals requires specific expertise in benchmark design.

items.title: Other infrastructure and use-case notes
points: TorchNeuron provides a native PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium hardware, enabling eager execution (immediate code evaluation) for research and debugging, released under Apache 2.0 license.
vLLM introduces push-based KV transfer to reduce time-to-first-token and time-per-output-token in distributed ('disaggregated') inference setups.
HUMXN AI lab subsidizes plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and cleaning services in Minneapolis, Chicago, and Miami to collect real-world robotics training data via wearable cameras.
Meta's 'Thin Orchestrator' architecture routes tasks to specialized AI agents without doing domain work itself, improving system reliability.
OpenAI reports major coding improvements for legacy languages like COBOL, Fortran, and Visual Basic, aiding software migration and modernization.

issues.subject: 😸 AI hackers left the door open

headlines: AI hackers broke into 100+ websites using exposed dashboards with no password protection, costing ~$50 in model fees per successful breach.
U.S. Homeland Security ordered federal agencies to remove DeepSeek products from systems over security concerns.
Anthropic neared a second $45B computing capacity deal with Nscale, one month after the first.

sections.title: AI Agents Targeting Real Websites Left Control Panels Wide Open
points: NorForge security researchers found 20+ exposed dashboards for Cairn, an AI agent tool used by criminals to break into online stores in the US, Japan, and Australia.

The hacking tool works by having multiple AI agents (software that autonomously takes actions like browsing sites or running code) collaborate on a shared whiteboard, with one 14-dashboard cluster holding 1,100+ active attack projects against online retailers.

Successful break-ins occurred in roughly 10% of attempts and took an average of 23 hours start-to-finish, costing attackers approximately $5 per attempt in model fees when averaged across all failures.

The dashboards contained unencrypted target lists, stolen login credentials, and operational notes—attackers left them accessible to the public internet with no password required, allowing researchers to spot hundreds of still-valid stolen passwords and API keys.

sections.title: Security Researcher Found Working Backdoor on Major Vendor's Website
points: NorForge confirmed one claimed compromised website—a large hardware parts vendor—had an active back door (hidden server page allowing file uploads) still live on the site.

Worker names and tool configurations in the exposed dashboards suggest attackers used DeepSeek's inexpensive V4.1 Flash model to power the agents, though this is NorForge's analysis rather than confirmed fact.
One attacker group had a bug that corrupted site names (replacing 'w' characters, turning 'wholesale' into 'holesale'), making related panels easy to identify and track.

sections.title: What Happens Next for Businesses
points: Companies should audit login systems, file upload pages, and authentication checks—these are the 'boring holes' that AI agents find faster when scanning hundreds of attempts than manual testers.
If you use outside red teams (hired security testers), verify they're protecting their own AI dashboards and control panels, as legitimate security setups were also left exposed.
NorForge is working with Reuters to notify victims and attempt to take down dashboards through hosting providers.
The 10% success rate may increase as the underlying AI models improve, making these attacks more cost-effective for criminals.
